screens.large: In Phase 1, NRG and a data center partner review land options, existing grid access infrastructure, and environmental factors to confirm site readiness.

screens.screenSummary: Confirm essential site resources — fiber, water, and natural gas — are available.

nodes.title: Fiber Connection
nodes.content: Plan to bring premium, high-speed fiber access to data center.

nodes.title: Water Supply
nodes.content: Ensure reliable water supply for responsible data center cooling, exploring all options for additive water solutions that benefit surrounding areas.

nodes.title: Natural Gas Supply
nodes.content: Verify reliable natural gas supply to keep data center powered.

screens.screenSummary: Start early coordination, applications, and agreements related to power needs.

nodes.title: Load Ramp Plan
nodes.content: Outline equipment and server installation stages related to power ramping to inform the Transmission Service Provider (TSP).

nodes.title: TSP & ISO Engagement
nodes.content: NRG engages with local Transmission Service Provider (TSP) on grid connection requirements for data centers and new BYOP. Independent System Operator (ISO) requirements for collocated load & generation are also evaluated.

nodes.title: Application Materials Review
nodes.content: NRG reviews load materials and formulates generation materials before submission to the Transmission Service Provider (TSP) and/or Independent System Operator (ISO).

nodes.title: Turbine Reservation
nodes.content: NRG leverages 5.4 GW of H-Class CCGT turbine slot reservations with in-service dates between 2029 and 2032 with leading equipment manufacturer GE Vernova.

screens.screenSummary: Review land use, environmental, and community factors for site readiness.

nodes.title: Land + EnvironmentalEvaluation
nodes.content: Require formal evaluations of land and environment — study assessments, surveys, reports — to confirm site readiness.

nodes.title: Lower-Carbon Options
nodes.content: Discuss lower-carbon power goals with customer — hourly match, 24/7, onsite or market-based RECs — and set timeline to reach goals.

nodes.title: Community Alignment
nodes.content: Engage local stakeholders, officials, and residents to inform development plans, address concerns, and support the approval process.

nodes.title: Air Permitting
nodes.content: NRG obtains necessary permits to ensure operations meet clean air standards.

nodes.title: CCS Studies
nodes.content: If desired by customer, NRG conducts preliminary Carbon Capture & Sequestration (CCS) feasibility studies.

screens.large: In Phase 2, approvals and agreements are secured to establish grid connection to site.

blocks.heading: Site + Grid Reviews
blocks.content: Review site power needs, grid capacity, and potential future upgrades.

blocks.heading: Load Request to TSP
blocks.content: Submit official request with Transmission Service Provider (TSP) to connect data center to grid, including electrical drawings, MW quantities, site plans, load ramps, and proof of land access.

blocks.heading: TSP Agreement + Deposit
blocks.content: TSP completes load study to identify if upgrades are needed and issues interconnection agreement. Agreement is signed and deposit provided, with NRG supporting review and coordination.

blocks.heading: Long-Lead Orders
blocks.content: NRG may pre-order long-lead equipment through TSP to prevent project delays.

blocks.heading: Permitting + Entitlements
blocks.content: Developer secures permits to build and operate data center and confirms land ownership and access rights.

blocks.heading: BYOP Plan
blocks.content: NRG works with data center to customize BYOP plan.

blocks.heading: BYOP Interconnection Applications
blocks.content: NRG submits BYOP characteristics and technical details to Independent System Operator (ISO).

blocks.heading: Full Interconnection Study
blocks.content: NRG works with ISO to complete full interconnection study, ensure safety standards are met, and sign agreement with deposit to fund infrastructure needed to connect plant.

blocks.heading: BYOP Equipment Orders
blocks.content: NRG finalizes long-lead equipment for BYOP plant and associated electrical infrastructure.

screens.heading: Bridge Power Solution
screens.content: NRG brings speed to power for data centers using a phased deployment strategy that leverages third-party bridge power solutions when grid power or necessary equipment is unavailable.

screens.large: In Phase 3, data center buildings and BYOP are constructed and connected to supporting infrastructure.

screens.screenSummary: Coordinate interconnection, track timelines, and manage delivery of major equipment and BYOP.

nodes.title: Load InterconnectionCoordination
nodes.content: NRG coordinates load interconnection and tracks timelines for infrastructure as Transmission Service Provider (TSP) builds upgrades, if needed, like substations, transmission lines, distribution lines, and protection schemes.

nodes.title: BYOP Construction
nodes.content: NRG manages BYOP construction with an Engineering, Procurement, and Construction (EPC) company, like Kiewit, and oversees interconnection to grid. Through the NRG x Kiewit partnership, established labor agreements provide price and schedule certainty.

screens.screenSummary: Build data center shells, data halls, and supporting infrastructure on site.

nodes.title: Site Mobilization
nodes.content: NRG mobilizes construction crews, equipment, and materials onto site to begin construction.

nodes.title: Data Hall Construction
nodes.content: Third party constructs and outfits data halls where servers will run.

nodes.title: Natural Gas Infrastructure
nodes.content: NRG constructs natural gas infrastructure needed to supply Combined-Cycle Gas Turbine (CCGT) plant, bridge power units, or backup systems.

nodes.title: Equipment Delivery
nodes.content: NRG manages delivery of major power equipment, turbines, and transformers to site for installation.

nodes.title: Shell Construction + Facilities
nodes.content: Main data center shells are constructed by third parties along with supporting facilities such as backup generation, fiber and connectivity, water processing, administrative buildings, and detention ponds.

screens.large: In Phase 4, grid interconnection and BYOP support load ramping as servers are installed and tested.

blocks.heading: Grid Interconnection Live
blocks.content: NRG, data center, and Transmission Service Provider (TSP) coordinate grid interconnection, enabling data center to draw power directly from grid.

blocks.heading: Bridge Power Online (Optional)
blocks.content: If required, NRG brings bridge power online before BYOP or full grid interconnection to maintain operations until permanent power is available.

blocks.heading: Phased Power Delivery and Ramp
blocks.content: Developer installs servers, runs tests, and gradually increases power use as equipment comes online.

blocks.heading: BYOP Online
blocks.content: NRG completes and commissions BYOP and coordinates metering to deliver energy to both the grid and data center.

blocks.heading: Full-Capacity Ramp
blocks.content: Developer continues adding servers and scaling up until data center reaches full capacity, enabled by BYOP.

blocks.heading: CCGT Supplement
blocks.content: NRG supplements and complements grid power with Combined-Cycle Gas Turbine (CCGT) generation.

screens.large: In Phase 5, data center operates at full capacity with continuous power and energy support.

screens.screenSummary: Deliver reliable power, optimize operations, and advance low-carbon performance.

nodes.title: Retail Power + Support
nodes.content: NRG provides retail power solutions tailored to customers, including hedging for risk mitigation, demand response, strategic services, and emissions tracking.

nodes.title: Lower-Carbon Options
nodes.content: NRG advances progress on data center low-carbon goals.

nodes.title: BYOP Operations
nodes.content: NRG delivers robust asset monetization solutions that optimize natural gas BYOP alongside grid power for reliable and flexible supply.

screens.large: The data center is fully operational. Step inside to see how everything comes together — from servers and cooling to power, people, and sustainability.

blocks.heading: Security
blocks.content: Layered security measures — badges, biometrics, cameras — protect both physical and digital assets inside the facility.

blocks.heading: Data Hall Operations
blocks.content: Inside the data halls, thousands of servers run workloads nonstop, supported by data center staff monitoring performance 24/7.

blocks.heading: HVAC + Airflow
blocks.content: HVAC systems circulate and filter air, maintaining stable climate conditions across the facility.

blocks.heading: Cooling Systems
blocks.content: Water-cooled systems and advanced HVAC regulate temperature to keep servers running efficiently.

blocks.heading: Grid Interconnection
blocks.content: This is where utility power flows into the site. NRG manages timing, load coordination, phased energization, and export of power to the grid in times of need.

blocks.heading: Fiber Connectivity
blocks.content: High-speed fiber connections link the data center to the world, enabling low-latency communication across global networks.

blocks.heading: Battery Systems
blocks.content: Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) and backup generators stand ready to provide instant power during outages.

blocks.heading: Power Management
blocks.content: Intelligent systems decide when to charge, discharge, or balance grid input — improving site-wide efficiency.

blocks.heading: Onsite Staff
blocks.content: Teams work around the clock in hall offices and support areas to ensure uptime, security, and customer service.

blocks.heading: Control Room
blocks.content: The “nerve center,” where operators track energy use, cooling, and reliability in real time.

blocks.heading: Sustainability
blocks.content: Onsite renewables, lower-carbon pathways, and emissions tracking tools reduce the environmental footprint of operations.

blocks.heading: Water Processing
blocks.content: Water is treated, cooled, and reused to reduce waste while providing consistent cooling for equipment.

blocks.heading: Sleeved Renewable Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs)
blocks.content: Seamlessly integrate off-site renewables into the data center power agreement, with all settlement and management processes handled on behalf of customers.

blocks.heading: Renewable Energy Credits (RECs)
blocks.content: Cover unmatched usage with unbundled Green-e certified RECs, including options for asset- or state-specific certificates.

blocks.heading: 24x7 Carbon-Free
blocks.content: Measure and demonstrate carbon-free usage on an hourly basis through renewable PPAs with grid consumption data.

blocks.heading: Certified or Renewable Natural Gas
blocks.content: Fuel BYOP with certified or renewable natural gas to decrease Scope 2 emissions.

blocks.heading: Onsite Solar or Battery Energy Storage System (BESS)
blocks.content: Deploy solar and/or battery storage by leveraging available land and interconnection for renewable energy with clear deliverability and additionality.

blocks.heading: Hydrogen-capable Solutions
blocks.content: Blend blue or green hydrogen into combined-cycle gas turbine fuel streams to provide lower-carbon, dispatchable power.

blocks.heading: Carbon Capture & Sequestration (CCS)
blocks.content: Apply carbon capture and sequestration technologies to abate residual emissions from natural gas combustion.

blocks.content:
Onsite generation is the production of energy at the point of use – the site where it is to be consumed.

It is a form of decentralised energy, enabling a business to make and use its own energy at a particular location, rather than buying that energy through the grid.
